subject: Host 'file not found' after a restore: NFS negative-lookup cache on the reader, fixed by lookupcache=positive
cluster: kind-ax-next-dev (OrbStack kernel 7.2.9), dev NFS server 10.96.200.49 (ax-next-memory-nfs, btrfs-backed /exports), fresh export dir /nfs-cache-test

nfs_version.kind: vers=4.2 on every mount (the dev server runs rpc.nfsd -N 3: NFSv3 is disabled, so nfsvers=3 could not be pinned here)
nfs_version.prod: vers=3, hard, proto=tcp (Filestore). The Linux client's lookupcache handling is the same code path for v3 and v4 (dentry revalidation in fs/nfs/dir.c), so the v4.2 result carries over; this is an inference, not a v3 measurement.

setup.writer: pod with an inline nfs: volume, rw
setup.reader_inline: pod with an inline nfs: volume, readOnly: true; /proc/mounts: nfs4 ro,relatime,vers=4.2,hard,proto=tcp,timeo=600,retrans=2 (default lookupcache) -- the shape the host's user-files-read volume has today
setup.reader_pv: pod with a PVC bound by volumeName to a static PV: accessModes [ReadOnlyMany], Retain, storageClassName "", mountOptions [lookupcache=positive], nfs readOnly: true; PVC mounted readOnly: true; /proc/mounts: nfs4 ro,...,vers=4.2,...,lookupcache=pos -- the shape the chart now renders
setup.server_writer: some trials write straight into the export on the NFS server pod instead of through the writer pod, so the writer is a genuinely different client (as the storage helper is in prod)

procedure: reader stats <f> -> ENOENT (negative dentry now cached)
1 s later the writer creates <f>; creation time taken on the writer
reader stats + opens <f> every 200 ms for 90 s from before the create; first success time recorded (same node, same clock)

trials.note: still ENOENT after 90 s of polling and minutes later; one readdir (ls) of the parent fixed it

summary.default_lookupcache: 3 of 5 visible after ~28.6 s (the parent dir's attribute cache, acdirmin 30 s, minus the 1 s gap); 2 of 5 NOT visible within 90 s. Polling the missing name never refreshes the parent's attributes, so the negative entry lives until something else (a listing, the attr timeout under other traffic) revalidates the directory.
summary.lookupcache_positive: 3 of 3 visible on the first poll after the create (161-185 ms = at most one 200 ms poll interval)
summary.conclusion: The stale ENOENT is the reader's cached negative dentry; lookupcache=positive removes it.
